**No, do not approve the $1,000-a-day spend plan.**

### Material Assumptions
- Your current Meta Ads campaign runs at $300/day generating a 3.2 ROAS ($58 revenue per bottle at a 30% 3-month reorder rate).
- Your inventory is capped at roughly 4,000 bottles, and restocking takes 10 weeks (approx. 70 days).
- You have $45,000 total ad budget through December 31.

### Why the $1,000-a-Day Plan Fails
Jumping spend from $300 to $1,000 a day ($30,000 a month) burns through your entire $45,000 budget in less than 45 days. At $58 a bottle, $1,000 daily ad spend will rapidly exhaust your 4,000-bottle inventory well before December 31. Because manufacturing takes 10 weeks, you will hit an absolute supply constraint, run completely out of stock, and miss the peak of Black Friday and holiday shopping. 

### Concrete Next Steps
1. **Calculate the Supply-Safe Spend Limit:** Determine the maximum daily spend that matches your remaining inventory (4,000 bottles) against your 70-day restock lead time, ensuring you do not stock out before new inventory arrives.
2. **Fix the Creative Before Scaling:** Do not increase spend blindly; ensure your ad creative and landing page are fully optimized to maintain or lower your Customer Acquisition Cost before pushing higher volume.
3. **Control the Inventory Flow:** Place your 10-week manufacturing reorder immediately to secure stock for the post-holiday period.

### Decision Criteria
Approve spend increases only when supply matches demand. If you cannot secure an expedited manufacturer restock to support 4,000+ additional bottles by November, hold daily spend at a level that preserves inventory through the 10-week lead time, or risk severe out-of-stock losses during peak season.
